UNMET: [fix-code] RQFROM-4 | WHY: The flat-file auto-resume `elif` in `core/pipeline/runner.sh` has no `--from-stage` guard. When `ZBUILD_STATE_FILE` is set and the state file has `status=in_progress` with a fresh timestamp, `get_resume_recommendation` returns `auto_resume`, the `elif` branch fires and sets `resume_mode=true` before the post-auto-resume `--from-stage` guard is reached. Because `resume_mode=true`, the guard (`if [[ -n "$from_stage" ]] && ! $resume_mode`) never fires, and the runner exits 0. The test failure confirms it: `pipeline-resume-test.sh` sub-test "integration: --from-stage without --resume exits 1" receives exit 0 on `in_progress` state. | QUOTE: `--from-stage <s>` works only when `--resume` is given. Without `--resume` the run refuses with a reason ("only valid with --resume") and does not start, even when the run would otherwise resume by itself.

ANSWER issue-acceptance finding 1: wrong — The build stage argued S5 and pipeline-resume-test.sh are mutually incompatible, so the finding should be dismissed. Re-examining now: the failing test proves RQFROM-4 is still unmet. The code comment in `core/pipeline/runner.sh` explicitly states the guard is "narrowed to interrupted-status only: status=in_progress runs are allowed to reach auto-resume so the DSFSTG-1 skip_restore=false branch continues to work (S5 in from-stage-rehydrate-test.sh uses in_progress for this)." That design choice causes the flat-file auto-resume `elif` to set `resume_mode=true` for `in_progress` state without a `from_stage` guard, and the pipeline exits 0 instead of 1. The test reports `expected: 1, got: 0`. RQFROM-4 is unmet; the finding holds.

ANSWER issue-acceptance finding 2: wrong — The build stage says `run-status-text.sh` is linked to `descriptive-id-readers-test.sh` in the acceptance test list. That shows the new behaviour is now asserted, but it does not make the change required by this issue. No requirement in RQRESU-*, RQFROM-*, RQADR-*, RQHYDR-*, RQLOOP-*, RQPATH-*, or RQGUAR-* names run-status-text.sh or its rendering behaviour. The change remains unasked. The finding holds.

ANSWER lens-correctness-code finding 2 (opened by review_lenses): wrong — DSCMBR-1's contract specifies the scenario where `build` is complete and `test` is aborted within iter k; the test correctly exercises that scenario and its assertions hold. The all-complete-in-iter edge case the finding describes (`_cid_nc=0` with an iter entry already present) is a different scenario not named by any RQXXX requirement in this issue. No requirement asks for Scenario B coverage.
